intro.title: Type Assertions, Non-null & satisfies
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple program that safely processes user input data, such as a name and age, using TypeScript's type safety features. You will learn to use type assertions to tell TypeScript the specific type of a value when you know more than the compiler, the non-null assertion operator to confidently access values that are not null or undefined, and the satisfies operator to ensure an expression matches a type without changing its inferred type. The main technologies are TypeScript's type system and its special syntax for assertions. This will help you write more robust and predictable code by explicitly managing types in your applications.
intro.usecase: Type assertions, non-null operators, and the satisfies operator are essential when working with external data sources like APIs or user inputs where TypeScript can't infer types automatically. For example, when building a dashboard that displays real-time analytics from a third-party API, you might use type assertions to tell TypeScript that the incoming data matches your expected chart format. In form validation scenarios, the non-null assertion operator helps safely access DOM elements after confirming they exist, while satisfies ensures configuration objects for UI components like modals or filters have the correct structure without widening types unnecessarily.
